perspective:
Mason Hurley’s accessible perspective:

- He is an accountant at a small community center. Martha Moua is a colleague there, a personal care aide; their relationship is professional and mainly work-related.
- He reviewed the community center’s financial reports and noticed discrepancies: healthcare expenses seemed unusually high and did not match usual spending patterns. This made him suspicious and anxious that Martha might be mismanaging funds.
- He spoke with Martha. He asked to discuss the recent financial report because numbers did not add up. Martha said there was likely a reasonable explanation and asked what discrepancies he meant. He pointed to the unusually high healthcare expenses. Martha said there might have been a misentry and that she would review and correct any errors.
- After that discussion, Mason concluded the discrepancies were a simple clerical error, not mismanagement. He felt relieved but embarrassed about his initial suspicion. He told Martha he appreciated her quick clarification, apologized for suspecting her, and said he should have asked her first. Martha said errors happen, understood his thoroughness, and suggested double-checking entries next time.
- He later believed Martha was competent, but that recurring clerical errors showed the current financial management system was inadequate. He felt frustrated with the system and empathetic toward Martha. He discussed preventing future errors with her, said the issue was the system rather than her management, and proposed creating a new, more robust financial system. Martha agreed to help and said it should address the gaps they identified.
- He drafted the new financial system proposal. He was hopeful it would benefit operations but uncertain whether management would approve or implement it. He told Martha this. Martha said it was a solid proposal, encouraged presenting it confidently, and said the benefits were clear. He asked her to help gather data to strengthen their case, and she agreed.
- After presenting the proposal to management, Mason thought the presentation went well. He felt satisfied with his efforts but physically and mentally exhausted, and believed he had done everything possible to advocate for the new system. He said it was now up to management. Martha praised his work and suggested he take a break. He planned to take a few days off to recharge and reflect, hoping for good news. Martha wished him well and offered to help while he was away.
- From Mason’s perspective, management’s final decision on the proposal is still pending; he has not been shown any decision yet.
